clue.text: Look, no hands!

parts.note: the cry of a show-off cyclist, reread as a timepiece you look at whose face has no hands, only a numeric display

explanation.surface: A child showing off by riding a bike without holding the handlebars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look' is a glance at the time, and 'no hands' is the defining feature of a timepiece with a numeric display rather than a dial.
explanation.definitionFit: A timepiece with a numeric readout has no rotating pointers, so you look at it and see no hands.

clue.text: Fabrics from plant in moisture-free setting

indicators.note: the plant sits inside the moisture-free setting, so one word is placed within the other

parts.note: moisture-free means dry
rape is a plant grown for oilseed

explanation.surface: Cloth produced from a crop grown in an arid environment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting' reads as surroundings, but it is the container, as a stone sits in a ring's setting; 'plant' is the oilseed crop, not a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: Drapery is the collective term for cloth and textile goods, as sold by a draper.

clue.text: Gateshead girls in see-through wear

parts.note: read as 'Gate's head': the first letter of Gate
lasses are girls, the word used in north-east England

explanation.surface: Young women from Gateshead dressed in transparent clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Gateshead is a town in north-east England; split as 'Gate's head' it gives the first letter G. 'see-through wear' is not sheer clothing but what you wear in order to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectacles are worn on the face to help the wearer see clearly through their lenses.

clue.text: Left it to chance anyway, being crafty

indicators.note: anyway means in any manner at all, so the letters may be put in any order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who trusted to luck, yet was clever about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anyway' scrambles L, IT and CHANCE into the answer. 'crafty' means relating to a craft or skill rather than cunning.
explanation.definitionFit: Something relating to the skills and methods of a particular craft or trade is called technical.

clue.text: All aglow at the smoking concert

definitions.meaning: smokers acting together have all put a match to their cigarettes

explanation.surface: Everyone glowing with pleasure at a concert where smoking was allowed.
explanation.walkthrough: A smoking concert was a Victorian men-only evening of music where smoking was permitted; here everyone has lit their pipes.
explanation.definitionFit: Illuminated means glowing with light, and smokers who have lit a cigarette have done the same thing.

clue.text: A number with two degrees in a state

parts.note: L is fifty in Roman numerals
AB is the American form of the Bachelor of Arts degree
AM is the American form of the Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: Someone with two university degrees living in an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: The degrees are given in American order, AB and AM rather than BA and MA, fitting a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabama is one of the fifty constituent states of the USA, in the Deep South.

clue.text: American city fashionable in the past

parts.note: chic means stylish or fashionable
ago means in the past, as in 'long ago'

explanation.surface: A US city that used to be stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicago is a major US city on Lake Michigan in Illinois.

clue.text: Dream-girl who gives one the go-by?

definitions.text: Dream-girl who gives one the go-by?

parts.words: Dream-girl who gives one the go-by?
parts.note: a girl you dream of who walks past you without stopping, a fancy that is going by

explanation.surface: A beautiful woman who ignores an admirer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' is a desire or a person you fancy; one who 'gives one the go-by' walks past, so is passing. The phrase means a short-lived enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief infatuation soon fades, like a dream-girl who walks straight past and is gone.

clue.text: Language upsetting Maria in a first-class compartment

indicators.note: the jumbled name is placed inside the compartment formed by the outer letters

parts.note: read as the first of 'class', its opening letter

indicators.note: upsetting means knocking over or disturbing, so the name's letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Upsetting a woman named Maria in a first-class railway carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' gives RAMAI; the 'first-class compartment' looks like a railway carriage, but 'first-class' gives only C, the first letter of class, and with 'a' forms the compartment.
explanation.definitionFit: Aramaic is an ancient Semitic tongue, spoken in the Near East in biblical times.

clue.text: Follower of Peter the Great in poor straits

indicators.note: poor means in bad shape, so the letters of the word are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A supporter of the famous Russian tsar who has fallen on hard times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges STRAITS; 'in poor straits' is the idiom for hard times.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter the Great was a tsar of Russia, so a supporter of him or his rule is a tsarist.

clue.text: For them it's mostly filling in time at work!

definitions.text: For them it's mostly filling in time at work!

parts.words: For them it's mostly filling in time at work!
parts.note: people whose working hours are spent stuffing dead animals, so 'filling' is literal

explanation.surface: Workers who mostly kill time on the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filling in time' suggests idling, but these workers literally fill skins with stuffing.
explanation.definitionFit: Taxidermists preserve dead animals by stuffing their skins, so their work consists of filling.

clue.text: Has a crush on one of the family?

definitions.meaning: treads on and squashes, rather than being infatuated
a relative: a spouse's son by an earlier marriage

explanation.surface: A family member who is infatuated with someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has a crush on' looks like infatuation but means treads on; split the answer 4,3.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepson is the son of one's husband or wife from a previous relationship, and so a family member.

clue.text: Bone of the body in solid formation

definitions.meaning: one of the small bones of a finger or toe
a close-packed body of troops or people

explanation.surface: A bone of the body in a tight cluster.
explanation.definitionFit: The finger and toe bones carry this anatomical name, and a tightly massed body of ancient Greek infantry bore the same name.

clue.text: Poet retracting on his agreement

parts.note: withdrawing consent is saying no
yes is the word of agreement

explanation.surface: A poet who goes back on something he agreed to.
explanation.walkthrough: Alfred Noyes (1880-1958) was an English poet, author of 'The Highwayman'. 'on' places one word before the other in an across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Noyes was an English writer of verse, best known for 'The Highwayman'.

clue.text: Invent a payment for hacks?

definitions.meaning: journalists are often paid per unit of text, a coin for each one

explanation.surface: Coming up with a way of paying journalists.
explanation.walkthrough: Hacks are journalists, paid by the word; 'coin' is money, so the phrase reads as cash for each word.
explanation.definitionFit: To coin a term is to invent a new expression, and a coin paid per unit of copy is a hack's fee.

clue.text: Not different from Iceland it could be revealed

indicators.note: the letters of the two words could be reshaped so the result is revealed

explanation.surface: Something that turns out to be just like Iceland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be revealed' rearranges ICELAND and IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that are exactly alike, with no difference between them, are identical.

clue.text: Top feature of a beauty queen, for what it's worth

definitions.text: Top feature of a beauty queen
definitions.meaning: her face is her highest-valued asset, at the top of her body
the apparent worth printed on a coin, note or stamp

explanation.surface: A beauty queen's best asset, whatever that is worth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for what it's worth' looks like a throwaway phrase but holds the second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The worth printed on a banknote or share is its nominal amount, and a beauty queen's prettiest feature is worth most.

clue.text: He gives a service and provides the fare

definitions.text: He gives a service and provides the fare

parts.words: He gives a service and provides the fare
parts.note: someone whose business is serving food and drink at events

explanation.surface: A man who runs a public service and collects or pays the fare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' and 'fare' suggest transport, a bus or taxi; here 'fare' is food and the service is at table.
explanation.definitionFit: A caterer supplies food and drink for functions, providing both the meal and its serving.

clue.text: Sufferers in adversity

parts.note: people who suffer harm or misfortune

explanation.definitionFit: Victims are people harmed by misfortune, crime or disaster.

clue.text: Cried into drink

indicators.note: the word is turned into something else, so its letters are rearranged to form it

explanation.surface: Someone weeping into a glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cried into' suggests tears falling into a glass; 'into' asks for CRIED made into a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Cider is an alcoholic drink made from fermented apple juice.

clue.text: Settle down to write

definitions.meaning: calm oneself, as in composing oneself

explanation.surface: Settling at a desk to begin writing.
explanation.definitionFit: To compose oneself is to become calm, and to compose a piece is to create it as an author or musician.

clue.text: Aspired to make American babywear

indicators.note: the letters of the word are used as material to make something new

explanation.surface: Someone ambitious to produce clothing for infants in the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' rearranges ASPIRED.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans call a baby's nappies by this name.

clue.text: Saw the cake wasn't sugar-coated

parts.note: wasn't means was not, giving the negative
iced means covered in sugar icing

explanation.surface: Spotting that the cake had no icing on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the cake' is scenery: a cake that was not iced.
explanation.definitionFit: To have noticed something is to have seen or observed it.

clue.text: Throw down the drain?

parts.note: to get rid of something, and also a trench that carries water away

explanation.surface: Discarding something down a drain.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is both a verb meaning discard and a noun for a drainage channel.
explanation.definitionFit: To ditch is to discard, and a ditch is a channel dug to drain water from land.

clue.text: Pat, I'm in arrangement of orchestral piece

indicators.note: an arrangement puts the given words' letters into a new order, as music is arranged

explanation.surface: A person called Pat agrees to join in a musical arrangement for orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement of' rearranges PAT, IM and IN; the 'piece' is an instrument, not a composition.
explanation.definitionFit: Kettledrums form part of the percussion section, so an orchestral instrument is a piece of its kit.

clue.text: To whom red roses were anathema in the Middle Ages

definitions.text: To whom red roses were anathema in the Middle Ages

parts.words: To whom red roses were anathema in the Middle Ages
parts.note: the white-rose side in England's fifteenth-century dynastic civil war hated the red rose of Lancaster

explanation.surface: Medieval people who hated red roses.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Wars of the Roses (1455-87) the house of York, badge a white rose, fought the house of Lancaster, badge a red rose.
explanation.definitionFit: Supporters of the house of York fought Lancaster, whose emblem was the red rose.

clue.text: Couldn't be meaner

parts.note: most stingy, as a superlative of tight-fisted

explanation.surface: Someone as miserly as it is possible to be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close' means stingy, so its superlative means meanest; read as a single definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Close means tight-fisted with money, so the superlative describes the stingiest person.

clue.text: Top insurance for motorcyclists?

parts.note: protection for the head of a rider, rather than the best insurance policy

explanation.surface: The best insurance deal for bikers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' is the head, and 'insurance' is protection against injury, not a policy.
explanation.definitionFit: Protective helmets guard a rider's head in an accident, insuring the top of the body.
